samples.uptimeSource: NSProcessInfo.systemUptime; same API as native lifecycle and smoke request receipts

limitations: OS target-window metadata is sampled, not continuous. On-screen flags do not prove uncovered pixels, compositor callbacks, physical HDR or A/V synchronization.

The frozen smoke starts untimestamped DOM pause/mute/subtitle/quality/seek/enhancement setup without an external readiness handshake. The observer cannot gate or prove window readiness before that setup.

Timestamped native menu/button requests are audited retrospectively against earlier completed OS queries for that exact window number. This is evidence of prior observation, not an interlock on the native action.

Intentional window resize, minimize, close, return and fullscreen transitions are allowed. No all-interval visibility claim is made; unchanged frozen native checks retain their own phase-specific window requirements.

RSS covers the observed runner process group, PPID descendants and retained known descendants; independently managed XPC services and GPU allocations are not attributable through this process-tree metric.
Competing-work detection covers named native/build programs, not arbitrary unrecognized model workloads. The run still requires serialized local GPU/model work.
Pins establish unchanged input files. The runner's --shared argument hashes a path; existing native linkage selects the loaded image. This observer does not claim loaded-image identity.
observer.scope: Unchanged frozen AppKit functional smoke with sampled session/display/resource observations and exact native-window request witnesses. No automatic retry.

callerPermissions.scope: Current caller only; no permission request or other-app permission claim.

preflight.uptimeSource: NSProcessInfo.systemUptime; same API as native lifecycle and smoke request receipts

attempt1.diagnosisScope: The original observation saw HDRPlayer only in the later named-process query, while its earlier ancestry tree still contained only the runner. Observer2 CPU regression reproduces that own-child-between-reads case. A separate disposable-child diagnosis reproduces Darwin EPERM before reap and absent group after reap; it is not a native lifecycle test.

cleanupDiagnosis.scope: Owned disposable sleeping Python children only; no native, model or build launch

cpuRegressionReport.scope: Nine CPU observer discovery/cleanup regressions, including one owned sleeping Python child; no player/model/build launch

preparation2.commandChange: Same frozen runner and native arguments; pinned .venv interpreter plus -B retained, only --output changes from native-floating-run-1 to fresh native-floating-run-2.
preparation2.environmentPolicy: Runner receives exactly this explicit environment, rather than ambient variables. The unchanged runner adds only METAL_DLSS_MPV_LIBRARY and HDRPLAYER_UI_SMOKE_KIND/REPORT, HDRPLAYER_LIFECYCLE_LOG, HDRPLAYER_FLOATING_VIDEO for the native child. No DYLD, Vulkan or shader lookup override is introduced.
protocol: One floating-video invocation, no controls scenario and no automatic retry.
Fresh positive matching-console session, unlocked state, awake active displays and at least 8 GiB disk before launch; sample the same display configuration and session throughout the bounded run.

Daemon-thread query watchdog at 1.5 seconds, observation completion gap at most 2 seconds, 130-second outer execution deadline; cleanup covers the entire inherited runner group even if its leader has exited.

Require at most 4 GiB observed runner process-tree RSS and no competing named native/build process. Retain target-PID-only CGWindow number/bounds/onScreen/alpha/layer metadata, never window titles or pixels.
Retain complete native lifecycle rows and native floating-window snapshots. Permit intentional main-window minimize/close, return, resize and fullscreen transitions.

Compare each timestamped native menu/button request with a completed earlier OS observation of the corresponding actual window number. Both sides use NSProcessInfo.systemUptime. This checks prior observation retrospectively; it does not gate native dispatch.
Frozen smoke acceptance, stdout/stderr, dom.json, lifecycle.jsonl and runner report.json remain unchanged and retained on success or failure.
Pin all original runtime/model/fixture/runner resources plus original manifest, probe, interpreter, observer and preparation receipt before/after execution.
changes: If the second process observation sees a new HDRPlayer, refresh process identity and bind only one descendant with an unbroken PPID chain to the runner, the original runner PGID, and proc_pidpath equal to the archived executable. Refresh the bound PID window metadata within the same bounded query; unknown competitors are never ignored.

Poll/reap the runner before killpg(0), retry a racing EPERM after polling again, and consult a fresh group inventory for persistent EPERM. Only a reaped leader plus an empty inventory establishes disappearance; live or unknown groups remain failures at the bound.
Always attempt runner.wait even if a group query or signal fails. Signal only the original owned runner group, preserving the prior no-escaped-PID-signals policy.

Prepare nine CPU regressions: startup between reads, unrelated process, wrong ancestry, wrong executable, disappearing unknown process, deterministic poll/exit EPERM race, persistent live-group EPERM, wait despite query failure, and one disposable own CPU sleep process. Root runs them; no model/native test was executed during preparation.

originalFailure.cause: The first process read predated native child startup; the later readiness probe saw the own child and rejected it as a competitor without reconciling ancestry.
originalFailure.cleanupCause: Darwin killpg(0) returned EPERM for the exited unreaped leader after TERM; root reproduced this with owned CPU children and confirmed the original PIDs were gone.
originalFailure.nativeFunctionalAcceptance: Not reached. First player.log is empty; all failed attempt outputs remain preserved.

unresolvedGuardLimitations: The frozen smoke has no external start handshake. Earlier DOM pause/mute/subtitle/quality/seek/enhancement setup is untimestamped and may precede the first OS target-window sample; this observer cannot qualify or prevent that startup gap.

Prior window observation is not proof of uninterrupted visibility or visibility at the later request; no all-interval visibility, uncovered-pixel, compositor, physical HDR, A/V synchronization or physical-input qualification is claimed.
Named-process detection cannot identify arbitrary unrecognized model programs. Process-tree RSS does not include independently managed XPC services or directly measure GPU allocations.
Input file pins and static native linkage do not prove loaded-image identity.
Observer2 has received AST/static inspection only; its CPU regressions and native execution remain unexecuted pending root validation.

Unexpected descendants outside the original runner group fail the observer and are recorded for root inspection. They are not signaled by previously observed PID because PID lifetime identity is not pinned.

limitations: OS target-window metadata is sampled, not continuous. On-screen flags do not prove uncovered pixels, compositor callbacks, physical HDR or A/V synchronization.

The frozen smoke starts untimestamped DOM pause/mute/subtitle/quality/seek/enhancement setup without an external readiness handshake. The observer cannot gate or prove window readiness before that setup.

Timestamped native menu/button requests are audited retrospectively against earlier completed OS queries for that exact window number. This is evidence of prior observation, not an interlock on the native action.

Intentional window resize, minimize, close, return and fullscreen transitions are allowed. No all-interval visibility claim is made; unchanged frozen native checks retain their own phase-specific window requirements.

RSS covers the observed runner process group, PPID descendants and retained known descendants; independently managed XPC services and GPU allocations are not attributable through this process-tree metric.
Competing-work detection covers named native/build programs, not arbitrary unrecognized model workloads. The run still requires serialized local GPU/model work.
Pins establish unchanged input files. The runner's --shared argument hashes a path; existing native linkage selects the loaded image. This observer does not claim loaded-image identity.
observer.scope: Unchanged frozen AppKit functional smoke with sampled session/display/resource observations and exact native-window request witnesses. No automatic retry.

teardownEvidence.scope: Raw ordered lifecycle receipts show host retention, detached floating window, empty child/layer arrays, worker destruction and final flush. The frozen runner rejected native acceptance before running its teardown assertions; these receipts are not relabeled as a passed runner check.

priorWindowObservationCrosscheck.reason: The observer stopped at failed frozen native acceptance before its retrospective request-observation audit.
priorWindowObservationCrosscheck.method: Same source predicate: visible exact target window number fully inside an awake display, with completed OS query end uptime at or before native request uptime.
priorWindowObservationCrosscheck.limitation: The first seekForward on second floating panel has no prior completed OS window observation. This is additional evidence scope, not the recorded native failure.

counterInterpretation.submitted-frames: Source mapping is next accepted frame ID/count.
counterInterpretation.completed-frames: Source mapping is the output emitted count, not a complete GPU-future inventory.
counterInterpretation.pending-frames: Source mapping is pending_count plus one when preview_emitted. It includes accepted inputs not yet emitted and can include output whose future already completed.
counterInterpretation.cause: No causal diagnosis or GPU busy/idle state is established by this export. The frozen strict pending==0 predicate remained unsatisfied.

sanitization.repositoryPaths: Workspace prefixes removed; retained repository-relative paths identify artifacts and source.
sanitization.externalPaths: Private home and temporary paths replaced by symbolic names; fixed system-tool paths retained.
sanitization.titles: All fields named title are redacted, including fixture metadata. OS target-window collection did not request window titles or pixels.
sanitization.serials: UIDs and serial/UUID metadata removed or replaced.
sanitization.objectIdentity: ObjectIdentifier pointers consistently replaced by per-export object labels, preserving equality relationships.
